status: The full odd-minus bound is supplied on the original host. The complementary window estimate and the uniform generic size bound are recorded separately.

retained_foundations: For the generic arithmetic count, the product of the eligible primitive parts must satisfy the logarithmic size inequality in PropGK uniformly in the twist, field of the character kernel and level. ETS9–11 give pointwise finiteness, an integer independent of the later coefficient data, its exact minimal valuations, and the local restrictions at every eligible prime. ETS12–14 resolve the stated vanishing and bounded-parameter cases.

On the linked ordinary-family route match the prime-to-order arithmetic seed and the rank-two CM twist to the integral Hecke support. The required supported primes below the characteristic-prime curves, the ensuing exceptional transfers and classicality must yield the weight-zero and both-rank statements at one mark. See ETS4–6 and the comparison with the pinned Brox reconstruction.

For the direct original-window approach the order product P(E,t) of ETS19 still needs the indicated size bound. ETS18 supplies the entire odd-minus summand including the primes dividing the degree. The dyadic and same-parity pieces of the direct product remain to be bounded on the same family.

formal_consumer.scope: The module gives the exact primitive valuation criterion on generic orbits, proves finiteness at all primes, and proves the full odd-minus bound on every original abelian CM host by the higher special-value formulas. ETS19 estimates the cost of replacing the remaining strict sum by the dyadic and complementary odd K-group orders. The size of that product on the chosen windows, or the uniform generic estimate together with the other source cases, remains a quantitative question.
